source.title: Compute-Optimal Network Design for Echocardiography Myocardial Segmentation and Perfusion Quantification using Neural Scaling Laws
source.authors: Clara Rodrigo Gonzalez; Matthieu Toulemonde; L. Gvinianidze; C. A. Smith; Oscar Bates; R. Senior; F. S. Ng; Meng-Xing Tang

record.tranche_reason: Applies neural scaling analysis to medical-image segmentation, a new modality and task, and reports scaling and extrapolation results.
record.gate_note: The study tests dataset-size scaling and cross-dataset prediction for image-segmentation loss. It does not test language-model pretraining loss, token or compute scaling, or a fixed-compute parameter/token allocation. Segmentation benchmark comparisons and perfusion-quantification results are not rows because they do not measure the scaling behavior itself.
record.test_reason: The study fits a dataset-size power law to U-Net test BCE loss on image subsets (500–5000) and checks its prediction at 10,000 images. This is a new setting (medical-image segmentation) bearing on V5 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a Chinchilla-style law fitted on data subsets predicts relative (not absolute) full-dataset performance and guides selection of much smaller architectures (240x fewer parameters than CompSeg). They also conclude that the law transfers across domains for relative performance, so costly domain-specific scaling analysis is not needed.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts a Chinchilla-style power law to U-Net image segmentation and BCE test loss, with dataset size measured in images. It uses a two-step fit, fixes the global αD, and does not test language-model token/compute scaling or a fixed-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The fit uses only 500, 1000 and 5000-image increments; the authors say this sparse sampling makes the fit sensitive to noise. Applying the CAMUS fit to CEUS produces a larger absolute-loss bias. Models below a minimum capacity threshold were excluded from fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: A dataset-size scaling law fitted on CAMUS B-mode predicts the ranking of CEUS losses across 15 U-Nets (ρ=0.793) but with a systematic absolute bias (β2=0.00562, p=2.55e-17).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling laws fitted on one dataset transfer across related datasets in relative but not absolute loss.

record.problems: The scaling fit uses only three dataset-size increments, which the authors say makes it sensitive to noise. Cross-domain absolute predictions show systematic bias, and the domain-specificity remains unexplored.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameters or compute (the model term is collapsed into a per-architecture constant A). Range beyond one decade of dataset size. Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes.
Depth and width are varied, but not at fixed parameter count; no shape comparison is reported.
The two-step fitting procedure is not compared with alternatives; no exponent sensitivity is reported.
Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested for language models; the only extrapolation here is a 2x dataset size in segmentation.
Not tested: no fixed-compute allocation is reported, despite the 'compute-optimal' title.
Not tested: no downstream performance as a function of scale is reported.

missing.what: Models below a minimum capacity threshold showed no dependence on dataset size and were excluded from fitting. This is a case where the power law fails; no count or values are given.
No goodness of fit of the power law on the 500/1000/5000 subset points, and no per-architecture fitted A or Dc, is reported.
The Discussion attributes intercept 0.0768 ± 0.0723 to CAMUS, but the Results give that intercept for CEUS (CAMUS intercept 0.134). The reported numbers are inconsistent.

record.verdict_notes: Despite the 'compute-optimal' framing, no compute or parameter scaling law is reported; the model-size term is absorbed into a per-architecture constant. BCE losses span a very narrow range (~0.664–0.676), so high rank correlation may reflect architecture ordering more than power-law fidelity. Segmentation-benchmark and perfusion results correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses image-segmentation BCE loss, not held-out language-model pretraining loss or scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
It extrapolates image-segmentation results, not language-model runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation is evaluated.
Depth and width are varied, but architecture effects are not isolated at a fixed parameter count.
Tests image segmentation on CAMUS and CEUS only; it does not test video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes beyond the reported cross-dataset prediction.
The study does not test downstream language-model task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
It reports limitations and domain-dependent prediction bias but does not compare alternative fitting choices or estimate how those choices change exponents or a compute-optimal split.

rows.subject: 15 U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fit a dataset-size scaling law to subset training results and predict full-dataset test BCE loss.
rows.measure: Agreement between predicted and observed full-dataset test BCE loss
rows.value: Spearman ρ = 0.950 (p = 6.09 · 10−8); regression slope = 0.799 ± 0.0549 and intercept = 0.134 ± 0.0366
rows.note: The authors report high correlation but note that the regression slope deviates from unity.
rows.check: Extrapolation is only 2x beyond the largest fit point, from three points with two free parameters per architecture. Ranking is predicted (ρ=0.950), but slope 0.799 shows absolute losses are not, as the authors state.

rows.subject: 15 U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Apply the CAMUS-fitted scaling law to predict CEUS test loss.
rows.measure: Agreement between predicted and observed CEUS test BCE loss
rows.value: Spearman ρ = 0.793 (p = 4.22 · 10−4); regression slope = 0.892 ± 0.108 and intercept = 0.0768 ± 0.0723
rows.note: The study describes cross-dataset generalization as partial; predicted and observed values correlate, but there is a systematic bias.
rows.check: Measures transfer of a CAMUS-fitted law to a different dataset, not whether the power-law form holds in CEUS. No version names cross-dataset transfer of a fit; moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: 15 U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Assess agreement between CAMUS-fitted predicted and observed losses using Bland–Altman analysis.
rows.measure: Bland–Altman agreement of predicted and observed test loss
rows.value: Mean difference (bias) = −6.13 · 10−4; 95% Limits of Agreement = −1.90 · 10−4 to 6.78 · 10−4; 93.3% of points inside the limits
rows.note: The text reports a slight negative systematic bias and larger differences at higher mean losses.
rows.check: Reported values are internally inconsistent: the bias (−6.13e-4) lies outside the stated 95% limits of agreement (−1.90e-4 to 6.78e-4), so the value cannot be read reliably.

source_check.problem: Faithfully transcribed, but the source's bias of −6.13 × 10−4 lies outside its stated agreement limits of −1.90 × 10−4 to 6.78 × 10−4; cannot_determine is appropriate.

rows.subject: 15 U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Assess agreement between CAMUS-fitted predicted and observed losses using Bland–Altman analysis.
rows.measure: Bland–Altman agreement of predicted and observed test loss
rows.value: Mean bias = 4.94 · 10−3; 95% Limits of Agreement = 2.93 · 10−3 to 6.95 · 10−3; 93.3% of points inside the limits
rows.note: The CEUS prediction has a higher systematic bias than the CAMUS result.
rows.check: Cross-dataset transfer bias, not a test of the power-law form; moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: 15 U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fit a shared-slope linear model with a modality-specific intercept to predicted and observed losses.
rows.measure: Difference in intercept between modalities (modalityCEUS coefficient)
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a statistically significant difference in response between modalities.
rows.check: Modality intercept difference concerns transfer of a fitted law across datasets, not any version; moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: U-Net architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Estimate the global dataset-scaling exponent while fitting the scaling law.
rows.note: The exponent was held constant in the architecture-specific second fitting step.
rows.check: A fitted exponent value alone does not show the power law holds. No goodness of fit on the subset points is reported. This is a fit parameter, not a result row.

source_check.problem: The exponent is a fitting parameter rather than an independent result establishing V5; retain as fit metadata.

relationships.condition: U-Net segmentation on CAMUS; dataset-size law fit on 500–5000 images, predicting 10,000
relationships.reason: R1: the fitted law predicts the model ranking (ρ=0.950), but slope 0.799 means absolute loss is mispredicted. The fit spans about one decade with three points. Text also says small models showed no dataset-size dependence and were excluded.
relationships.display_finding: Predicted model rankings achieved ρ=0.950, but a slope of 0.799 indicated inaccurate absolute losses; the fit used three points over about one decade and excluded small models without dataset-size dependence.

source_check.condition: U-Net segmentation on CAMUS; dataset-size law fit on 500–5000 images, predicting 10,000
source_check.reason: R1 shows strong rank prediction but incomplete absolute-loss agreement. Section 5 explicitly excludes low-capacity models showing no dataset-size dependence, qualifying applicability within this setting; sparse fitting alone would not establish a limitation.

relation.reason: Reports its own predicted-versus-observed loss measurements assessing the scaling law's applicability.

tranche.reason: Tests a power-law loss model in a new setting, medical-image segmentation, using subset fits and full-dataset predictions.

source_check.notes: Section 4.1 gives the CAMUS regression intercept as 0.134 ± 0.0366; Section 5 instead repeats the CEUS intercept, 0.0768 ± 0.0723, alongside the CAMUS slope. Extrapolation is only twofold beyond the largest fitted dataset, with three subset sizes and two architecture-specific fitting parameters.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The fitted law predicts full-dataset loss with high rank correlation, though the regression slope differs from unity (R1).
